journey.name: Memory Leak Check - Composer Surface
journey.description:
Verifies that opening and discarding the post composer and reply composer does not retain ViewModels or UI components across push/pop lifecycle events.
Executes 3 loop iterations with theme switches (dark/light) to trigger Activity recreation while observing LeakCanary output.
Bench note (2026-10-31): the reply composer opens with "Couldn't load reply target" because the bench fixtures can't resolve the replied-to post. The composer still opens and closes, so the push/pop is exercised, but the reply-target loading path is not.

actions.action: Verify that the app is open on the Home feed
Tap the Compose Floating Action Button to open the composer
Verify that the composer overlay is visible with text input focused
Type sample text into the post composer field
Tap the Add image button in the composer
In the system photo picker, select the first photo or video in the grid
Verify that the composer is visible again with a media attachment in the draft
Tap the Close composer button
Confirm Discard in the discard changes dialog
Verify that the composer closes and the Home feed is visible
Tap the Reply icon on the first post in the feed
Verify that the reply composer overlay is visible
Type reply text into the composer input field
Tap the Close composer button
Confirm Discard in the discard changes dialog
Verify that the composer closes and the Home feed is visible
Switch the device to dark theme
Switch the device back to light theme
Repeat all of the steps above two more times
Press the Home button to send the app to the background, then wait 15 seconds for LeakCanary analysis
Verify that no LeakCanary leak notification appears except for known accessibility delegate semantics cache
